question: The price of a bike increases to Rs. 100000 after 3 increases. The 1st increase being 11.11%, 2nd being 12.50% and the 3rd being 25%. Find the original price.
solution:
Given:

The first increase is 11.11%

The second increase is 12.50%

The third increase is 25%

After three increases the price of a bike becomes Rs 100000

Concept used:

Always remember 

11.11% = (1/9)

12.50% = (1/8)

25% = (1/4)

Solution:

Let us consider the price of a bake = Rs. P

For first increase 

P + (11.11% of P)

P + (1/9 × P)

P + P/9

(9P + P)/9 = 10P/9

For second increase 

⇒ (10P/9) + [12.5% of (10P/9)]

⇒ (10P/9) + [(1/8) × (10P/9)]

⇒ 10P/9 + 10P/72

⇒ 90P/72

For third increase

⇒ (90P/72) + (25% of 90P/72)

⇒ (90P/72) + (1/4 × 90P/72)

⇒ (90P/72) + (90P/288)

⇒ (360P + 90P)/288

⇒ 450P/288

According to the question,

450P/288 = 100000

P = (100000 × 288)/450

P = Rs. 64000

The answer is **64000**
